activities.title: Feelings Faces
activities.description: Take turns making a face for a feeling (happy, sad, surprised, scared) and guessing which one the other is showing.
activities.example: Dad scrunched up his face in mock horror, and Priya guessed "surprised!" on the first try.
steps: Whisper a feeling to yourself, then make that face
Have your child guess the feeling
Swap turns and keep going

activities.title: Kindness Catch
activities.description: Toss a soft ball back and forth, and each time you catch it, say one kind thing about the other person.
activities.example: Every catch came with something kind -- "you always help me find my shoes" or "you make me laugh."
steps: Toss the ball to each other
Whoever catches it says something kind about the other person
Keep going for several rounds

activities.title: Balloon Breathing
activities.description: Practice slow, calming breaths together by pretending to blow up a balloon in your belly, then slowly letting it out.
activities.example: Three slow belly-breaths before bed, imagining a balloon filling up and slowly letting the air out.
steps: Place a hand on your belly
Breathe in slowly like filling a balloon
Breathe out slowly like letting the air out

activities.title: Gratitude Drawing
activities.description: Draw a picture of something you're thankful for and explain why.
activities.example: Zoe drew her dog and explained "because he always makes me laugh when I'm sad."
steps: Think of something you're thankful for
Draw a picture of it
Share why it matters to you

activities.title: Calm Down Jar
activities.description: Make a glitter jar together and shake it, watching it settle as a calming trick.
activities.example: Watching the glitter slowly settle helped Liam calm down after a frustrating moment at school.
materials: A clear jar or bottle, water, glitter, glue
steps: Mix water, a bit of glue, and glitter in a jar
Seal it tightly
Shake it and watch together whenever you need to calm down

activities.title: Three Good Things
activities.description: Before bed, each share three good things that happened today, however small, and why they mattered.
activities.example: "My friend shared her snack," "I landed that skateboard trick," "dinner was my favorite."
steps: Each think of 3 good moments from today
Share them and say why each one felt good
Make it a regular bedtime habit

activities.title: What Would You Do?
activities.description: Talk through a few "what would you do?" social scenarios, like a friend being left out, and discuss kind responses together.
activities.example: Talked through a friend being left out at recess -- decided inviting them over was kinder than ignoring it.
steps: Describe a simple social situation
Ask what they'd do and why
Talk through other options together, no wrong answers

activities.title: Worry Jar
activities.description: Write down a worry on a slip of paper and put it in a jar together, then talk about one small step to deal with it.
activities.example: Wrote down "scared about the spelling test" and agreed the next step was practicing 5 words a night.
steps: Write down something on their mind
Put it in the jar together
Talk through one small, doable next step

activities.title: Feelings Thermometer
activities.description: Draw a thermometer scale from calm to upset, and talk about where today's feelings land.
activities.example: Marking "a little frustrated" on the scale opened up a conversation about a tricky homework assignment.
steps: Draw a simple thermometer scale
Mark where you feel today
Talk about what's behind that feeling

activities.title: Compliment Circle
activities.description: Take turns giving each other one genuine compliment and explaining why.
activities.example: "You always help me when I'm stuck on something" made Dad's day.
steps: Take turns giving a genuine compliment
Explain why you picked it
Notice how it feels to give and receive one

activities.title: Values Compass
activities.description: Talk together about 3-4 things they really value (honesty, fairness, fun) and how those show up in their daily choices.
activities.example: Realized "fairness" was behind the decision to split the last cookie evenly with a sibling.
steps: Ask them to name a few things that matter most to them
Talk through a recent decision and which value it connects to
Notice together where values sometimes conflict, and how they chose

activities.title: Conflict Replay
activities.description: Talk through a recent disagreement (with a friend or sibling) and replay it, exploring a different way it could have gone.
activities.example: Replayed an argument over a video game turn, and agreed next time they'd set a timer instead of arguing.
steps: Pick a recent disagreement, calmly
Walk through what each side wanted
Brainstorm a version where both sides feel better about the outcome

activities.title: Tech-Free Check-In
activities.description: Spend 15 minutes phone-free together just talking about how their week is actually going, no fixing, just listening.
activities.example: Learned a friend group chat had been stressful all week -- just listening helped more than advice would have.
materials: None needed -- just put phones away
steps: Put all devices in another room
Ask open questions and really listen
Resist jumping in with advice unless they ask for it

activities.title: Gratitude Letter
activities.description: Write a short thank-you note to someone who's helped you, and consider sending it.
activities.example: Writing to a grandparent about a favorite memory together turned into a longer, heartfelt letter than planned.
materials: Paper and pen, or a notes app
steps: Pick someone who's helped you recently
Write a short note about why you're grateful
Decide together whether to send it

activities.title: Perspective Swap
activities.description: Talk through a recent disagreement from the OTHER person's point of view.
activities.example: Arguing their sibling's side of a recent disagreement helped them realize it wasn't as one-sided as it felt.
steps: Pick a recent disagreement, calmly
Each argue the OTHER side's point of view
Talk about what that changed, if anything

activities.title: Strengths Interview
activities.description: Take turns interviewing each other about a recent challenge and what strength helped you get through it.
activities.example: Realized "patience" was the strength that helped get through a hard math assignment.
steps: Think of a recent challenge, big or small
Interview each other about what helped you handle it
Name the specific strength you used

activities.title: Future Self Letter
activities.description: Each write a short letter to yourself one year from now, then (optionally) share a part of it with each other.
activities.example: Wrote "I hope you still play guitar" and sealed it to open again next birthday.
steps: Write a letter to your future self, one year ahead
Include a hope, a worry, and something you're proud of now
Seal it and agree on a date to open it together

activities.title: Hard Topic, Safe Space
activities.description: Pick one topic that's been hard to bring up and have a calm, no-judgment conversation about it together.
activities.example: Talked calmly about a dropping grade -- turned out the real issue was a tough new seating arrangement in class.
steps: Agree ahead of time this is a listening conversation, not a lecture
Let them share first, without interrupting
Share your own perspective calmly, and thank them for being honest

activities.title: Stress Debrief
activities.description: Talk through one stressful moment from the week and what helped (or would help) most.
activities.example: Talking through a stressful exam week revealed that just having someone to vent to helped more than advice did.
steps: Pick one stressful moment from the week
Talk through what happened and how it felt
Discuss what helped, or what might help next time

activities.title: Values in Action
activities.description: Talk about a recent choice and which personal value it reflected.
activities.example: Choosing to stay late and help a friend study reflected "loyalty" more than they'd realized in the moment.
steps: Pick a recent decision, big or small
Talk about what value was behind it
Notice if that value shows up in other choices too
